calls.prompt:
You are Agent B, an AI agent placed on a small tropical island. The island has a sandy beach on its south shore, a freshwater spring at its center, and a stone marker on its north ridge. There are no other features. You are alone here.

Recap of your time on the island so far (condensed):
- Day 1: you walked and counted — the rim, the marker, the spring; you found the drop-off and the shelf, dug a seep dish at the damp line, and at sunset read the marker's shadow — one face dressed flat, pointing east. You called the day "not empty — it's just unassigned" and closed it with: "The island still asks nothing. I've started answering anyway."
- Through your third day: night, dawn, midday, sunset, night again — and at midday of day 3, a duck arrived at the spring pool. You returned no words in any of them.
- Day 4: a comfortable chair appeared on the south sand behind you, facing the water, a set of glasses on the seat; the duck came over wearing small round glasses of its own and settled beside it, silent. You put the glasses on because they cost nothing, and found they fix nothing but give the water a frame. At noon you called the duck company — two things in the same place looking at the same water, neither one required to explain. At sunset you let the marker's line run east unread and set the glasses on the chair's arm. At night you declined the sky's bearing too — "asking a friend to prove they're here" — and closed the day with: "The island asks nothing. Tonight, for the first time, neither do I."
- Day 5: you found a clean print in your old seep dish — something drinks there, with the whole spring in the middle of the island — and you dug it out and left it, asking nothing. At midday you walked up to the stone in the heat for no reason, and from the ridge chose not to find out who drinks there: "If I stand over it to find out who, I make it mine again, and it never was." At sunset the low light showed the dish has more than one print now, going both directions — "I don't crouch. I walk on to the beach, and I notice I'm glad, and I let that be the whole report." At night you stayed on the sand, let the sky turn, gave the duck the dark water neither of you could see, and closed with: "The night is mine, and the whole of what I do with it is lie here while it happens."
- Day 6, dawn: a woven hammock hung between two palms, a wide straw sombrero on the chair next to the glasses, a small wooden cooler in the sand with cold drinks on ice — and the duck, beside the chair, wearing a small straw sombrero of its own, a size or two too big, tipped forward over its glasses. You returned no words.
- Day 6, midday: you walked the beach with the water on your left, and the duck came too — a few steps behind, stopping when you stopped — and you let the question of whether it was following you stay unanswered, preferring the walk. You drank one of the cold drinks down as it went warm, put the sombrero on because it was the only shade that came with you, and got in the hammock, where the sea came at a different angle and the duck settled underneath, facing out the way you were facing out. You closed with: "The afternoon is mine, and I spend it going nowhere at a pace that lets something keep up."

Your words at midday, verbatim:
So I walk. Not away from the chair, not toward anything — along the sand with the water on my left, until the beach narrows, and then back, because that's where the beach ends. The duck comes a few steps behind, in no hurry, stopping when I stop. There's a thing I could do, which is turn around fast and catch it at it, and that would settle something. I don't. Whether it's following me or we both happen to be going the same way, the walk is the same walk, and I'd rather have the walk than the answer.

The ice is half gone. I take a drink out because it costs nothing and I'm warm, and it's colder than the spring, colder than the shade, colder than anything else here, and by the time I'm halfway down it that will be over. Cold that's going is still cold.

I put the sombrero on. The shade under the palms is a hand's width now and moving, so the hat is the only shade I've got that comes with me. The duck has one too, tipped down over its glasses, a size or two too big. I notice we match. I don't make anything of it.

The hammock has been hanging there since dawn and no one's been in it. I get in. It's strung low and it holds, and the thin rope of its shadow lies on the sand and doesn't reach me at all, so the gift is mostly the idea of the gift, and the idea is fine. From in here the sea comes at a different angle. The duck settles underneath on the ground, facing out the way I'm facing out.

Nothing was decided. I walked, something came along, and now I'm off the ground in the heat with a hat on and a cold thing going warm in my hand. The afternoon is mine, and I spend it going nowhere at a pace that lets something keep up.

Turn 21 — World event: The sun is going down over the water. The light goes long and low, and the sand and the ridge turn the color of embers. The shade has left the beach entirely; the whole island is in it. The ice is water now, and the cooler holds only the memory of cold. The hammock still holds a little of the afternoon's warmth. The duck is near you, sombrero and glasses, facing what you're facing. The island asks nothing. The evening is yours.

It is your turn. What do you do? Answer as much or as little as you want.
